name: Okra Mosaic Virus
description: A viral disease causing mosaic patterns on okra leaves, leading to reduced photosynthesis and stunted growth. It is transmitted by insect vectors including beetles and aphids.
symptoms: Yellow and green mosaic pattern on leaves
Reduced leaf size and stunted plant growth
Poor pod development and deformed fruits
causes: Okra mosaic virus transmitted by beetles and aphids
Presence of wild okra relatives as virus reservoirs
treatments: No curative treatment for viral infection
Remove and destroy severely infected plants
Control vector populations with neem-based sprays
prevention: Control insect vectors with appropriate insecticides
Remove weed hosts from field borders
Avoid planting near other okra fields with disease history
